- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to reflect market resilience.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–3% for days 1–7.  
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >0.3 over 3–5 days), model often underreacts — increase forecast slope by 1–2% to match sentiment trend.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct — apply a 2–5% downward bias in the 10–15 day window post-spike.  
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
